title: Is the Market Missing the Point on Salesforce Inc (CRM)’s AI Positioning?
content:
Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) is one of the best stocks to buy in 2026 according to billionaire George Soros.

On May 1, Barclays named Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) as one of its top stock picks in the infrastructure software space amid the AI shift. According to the investment bank, AI is reshaping the enterprise software landscape, and Salesforce is among the companies that stand to benefit from this shift.Is the Market Missing the Point on Salesforce Inc (CRM)’s AI Positioning?

Pixabay/Public Domain

Pushing back on the concerns around AI disruptions of incumbent enterprise software vendors, Barclays said that AI will be an additive force, not a replacement. According to the investment bank, enterprise software incumbents like Salesforce have built a solid competitive position. The firm noted that this position is supported by data gravity, security and compliance standards, and switching costs.

For Salesforce in particular, Barclays noted that embedded workflows and a massive customer base have led to switching costs that shield the company amid AI integration into existing enterprise systems.

Barclays’ views on Salesforce and AI align with those of TD Cowen, which on April 24 identified Salesforce as a key beneficiary of enterprise AI adoption. According to TD Cowen, incumbent software vendors like Salesforce stand to benefit more from AI than markets currently reflect.

Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) is a provider of customer relationship management software. Its software is used in applications like sales, marketing automation, analytics, and customer service. Salesforce was founded in 1999 and is based in California.

While we acknowledge the potential of CRM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. That's where he seems to be. So he kind of is indicating if they're not managed well. Yeah.

That just gets swept up. He doesn't specify. He, you know, it's not like he

title: Anthropic CEO warns software companies can 'go bust' without AI
content:
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei warned that some software companies could "completely go bust" without AI integration while speaking at his company's The Briefing: Financial Services event.

Yahoo Finance Tech Editor Dan Howley breaks down Amodei's comments and what it could be signaling for software developers.

Video Transcript

00:00 Speaker A

Anthropic's Dario Amodei making headlines warning some software companies, he says, will completely go bust.

00:09 Speaker A

What does that mean?

00:11 Dan Howley

Uh he was having a conversation uh with Andrew Ross Sorkin and uh Jamie Dimon. And basically the conversation came down to what does this mean for the the SaaS-ocalypse, right? The software as a service apocalypse. and how we've seen those kind of stocks melt down the CRMs, the NOWs, the the Snowflakes. Uh and basically he said, you know, there there will be some that manage to evolve with uh the AI, you know, build out and there will be others that won't and they'll just kind of go the way of the dinosaur.

00:46 Speaker A

And is is he say and is he saying the moat there is, well, if if it if it's just that your software is complex and tough to write, you've got problems.

00:55 Dan Howley

That's it exactly. And it's you know, it's going to be more of uh what what what does that mean for what do you mean for customers? What do you have to offer? What's what's your key differentiator beyond just the software?

01:07 Speaker A

He's saying data or distribution or like customer relationship. That's what he's getting at.

01:12 Dan Howley

Yeah. And and, you know, this has been the the kind of ongoing question, what does this mean for software stocks? And you know, a bunch of people that I've spoken to have said, it doesn't mean that the bulk of them will just go poof, right? You're not going to wake up one morning and they're gone. A lot of them are already integrating AI.

01:29 Dan Howley

I mean, look at Service now. They already work with Nvidia, they're integrating AI uh into their their own services. And so that's something that I think we'll see a lot more companies do. Microsoft, by the way, does that with Copilot, whether or not that's, you know, super successful. I mean, we saw them report uh great growth as far as Copilot seats go when it comes to their enterprise or Microsoft 365. But you know, other companies are are are going to have to get on board as well.

01:52 Dan Howley

Obviously Salesforce has its own uh AI capabilities, but I I think that the fear is, you know, we just saw Anthropic talk about further uh pushing further into the uh financial services industry. So I think there's there's going to be this continued friction between, you know, the the companies, the established companies bringing in these AI companies like Anthropic, like Open AI, and then those very same companies offering their own similar product. And so it's going to be interesting to see how this shakes out.

02:22 Dan Howley

But the ones I think, you know, Dario Amodei is right that it'll be that the the differentiator will be the customer service, the support, not necessarily just the software.

02:33 Speaker A

Not just your software's tough to write. That's not going to get it done, he's saying.

02:35 Speaker A

Dan Howley, thank you, sir. Appreciate it.

title: Outreach Announces Integration with ServiceNow to Accelerate Revenue Execution Across the Entire Revenue Cycle
content:
New integration helps sellers reduce app switching, stay aligned across systems, and execute key sales activities without leaving ServiceNow CRM

SEATTLE, May 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Outreach, the agentic AI platform for revenue teams, announced a new integration with ServiceNow at Knowledge 2026. The integration brings revenue orchestration directly into ServiceNow’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM), enabling go-to-market teams to move faster, stay in flow, and take action across critical sales workflows. The integration enables revenue teams to execute key sales workflows across the full revenue motion in ServiceNow while keeping data aligned automatically between Outreach and CRM.

As a ServiceNow Build Partner, Outreach delivers a native bidirectional sync between Outreach and ServiceNow Sales CRM, keeping core customer and activity data dynamically updated so teams can operate with speed, accuracy, and consistency. The integration will be available in the ServiceNow Store.

With the integration, revenue teams can execute end-to-end agentic AI workflows and capture the activity directly inside ServiceNow Sales CRM. For sellers, this means less app switching and less manual work. For sales leaders and RevOps teams, this means clearer visibility into revenue activities across systems, streamlined execution of core revenue workflows, and a consistent path from engagement to opportunity close.

"Revenue teams need technology that drives action, not more complexity," said Abhijit Mitra, Chief Executive Officer at Outreach. "Our integration with ServiceNow helps sellers work more efficiently by reducing app switching, keeping data aligned across systems, and enabling key sales activities directly within ServiceNow CRM. Together, Outreach and ServiceNow help revenue teams execute faster across the entire revenue motion, so sellers can spend more time with customers and less time managing systems."

"Exceptional customer service is shifting from transactional to transformational, underpinned by intelligent, connected experiences powered by AI," said Alix Douglas, group vice president, Partner Solutions at ServiceNow. "Outreach's integration, built on the ServiceNow AI Platform, equips organizations to accelerate revenue execution by keeping sellers in flow, data aligned, and key activities moving - all without leaving ServiceNow CRM. Together, we're advancing a shared mission to supercharge every stage of the customer journey."

The ServiceNow Partner Program rewards partners for their broad expertise and experience to drive opportunities, reach new markets, and deliver transformative outcomes for joint customers across the enterprise. As a Build partner, Outreach develops and distributes applications with the ServiceNow AI Platform, including tailored configurations and seamless integrations to enhance platform capabilities.

Story Continues

About Outreach

Outreach, founded in 2014, is the only complete agentic AI platform for revenue teams. Outreach infuses agentic AI, conversation intelligence, and assistive AI to power hundreds of use cases across revenue motions. From new logo prospecting to expansions, deal acceleration, driving retention, and forecasting, Outreach AI automates workflows and frees sellers to focus on more strategic conversations and actions. Revenue leaders benefit from connected account visibility, performance insights, and higher forecasting accuracy across every GTM team. World leading enterprise organizations use Outreach to power their revenue teams, including Databricks, SAP, Siemens, and Verizon to name a few. To learn more, please visit www.outreach.ai.
